introduction: A visitor-facing downtown setting shaped by the square, hotels, shopping and cultural destinations.
union-square.characterHeading: A downtown destination, not one uniform retail market
character: The Recreation and Park Department documents the square’s longstanding retail, hotel and cultural role. The modern transit connection adds an address-specific access consideration.
union-square.fit: Compare this area when customer visits, hospitality and a recognizable downtown destination matter. Separate a street-facing retail requirement from an upstairs office search.
union-square.check: Walk from Powell or Union Square/Market Street station to the actual entrance. Compare street-facing retail and upstairs offices separately, and observe customer activity at your opening hours rather than assume visitor traffic translates into sales.
union-square.geography: Use the map to compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Approximate locations are not legal boundaries or a list of available premises.

introduction: A civic and cultural district where government buildings, ceremonial public space and performing-arts institutions give the area a distinct working-day and event setting.
civic-center.characterHeading: Government, culture and a historic public landscape
character: SF Planning identifies the Civic Center as a National Historic Landmark District and documents its historic landscape.
civic-center.fit: Worth comparing when proximity to civic institutions or cultural venues is useful to the work. Check the exact walking route, entrance and operating hours required by staff and visitors.
civic-center.check: Check the route between the premises, relevant institutions and transit at the times you use them. Compare office entrances, public-facing access and event schedules separately; nearby institutions do not establish demand for your business.
civic-center.geography: Use the map to compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Approximate locations are not legal boundaries or a list of available premises.

introduction: A neighborhood setting organized around retail streets and public space, with Patricia’s Green at Octavia Boulevard and Fell Street as a concrete landmark.
hayes-valley.characterHeading: Neighborhood streets and a public-space center
character: The Market and Octavia Area Plan provides the broader neighborhood and street-design context. Patricia’s Green is documented by the park operator as a picnic and playground space.
hayes-valley.fit: Compare for a customer-facing business that values a neighborhood street setting, or a small team that wants daily access to local public space. Evaluate the actual storefront and block.
hayes-valley.check: Check permitted use, deliveries, signage and access at the particular address. Separate a ground-floor shop from an upstairs office, and do not infer office suitability from a mixed-use residential building.
hayes-valley.geography: Use the map to compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Approximate locations are not legal boundaries or a list of available premises.

introduction: A dense community-serving commercial and retail setting, with the Chinatown–Rose Pak station at Stockton and Washington as a specific transit anchor.
chinatown.characterHeading: A distinct community and several commercial streets
character: SFMTA describes Chinatown as a historic hub of the city’s Asian community. The Planning Code describes the Community Business District’s transitional edges and an intent to accommodate modest local business growth.
chinatown.fit: Start with the customers and operating needs the business serves, then compare the exact street, entry and delivery arrangements. Distinguish core Chinatown from the Financial District and North Beach edges.
chinatown.check: Compare Grant Avenue, Stockton Street and the district edges individually. Confirm permitted use, signage, loading and any office-size restrictions for the actual premises; a district description is not an approval for your operation.
chinatown.geography: Use the map to compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Approximate locations are not legal boundaries or a list of available premises.

introduction: A neighborhood commercial setting anchored by Washington Square, sidewalk cafés and restaurants, and literary destinations near Columbus Avenue.
north-beach.characterHeading: A local commercial setting with a long cultural history
character: Recreation and Parks dates Washington Square to 1847. City Lights identifies its bookstore at Columbus and Broadway in North Beach.
north-beach.fit: Worth exploring for a customer-facing concept whose day-to-day operation fits a neighborhood destination setting. For office searches, inspect the actual building rather than assuming the area’s cultural identity establishes workspace quality.
north-beach.check: Check permitted use, acoustic privacy, entrance access and deliveries. A café or bookstore nearby may shape the working day, but it does not establish the suitability or availability of an office.
north-beach.geography: Use the map to compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Approximate locations are not legal boundaries or a list of available premises.

introduction: A park-based workplace setting where historic buildings, nature and a spread-out campus offer a distinct alternative to downtown streets.
presidio.characterHeading: Historic workplaces within a national park
character: The Presidio Trust documents adaptive reuse of former Army buildings and its role as landlord on federally owned land. Leasing income is reinvested in the park.
presidio.fit: Compare when access to outdoors and a campus-like environment matter to the team. Test the full commute to the particular building, including any shuttle connection and the final walk.
presidio.check: Check the exact building, shuttle and parking arrangements, and the Presidio Trust’s process for alterations. A park-based workplace can involve different access and fit-out arrangements from a downtown office.
presidio.geography: Use the map to compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Approximate locations are not legal boundaries or a list of available premises.

south-park.characterHeading: A smaller setting within the wider SoMa search

south-park.fit: Compare when immediate access to a compact outdoor gathering place is valuable to a team. Inspect the building, its light and layout, and the route to transit independently.
south-park.check: Compare the actual entrance, layout, daily access and nearby streets. Being close to the park does not establish office condition or available space. Keep this small pocket distinct from the wider SoMa search.

introduction: A neighborhood shopping corridor within the Marina, with a relatively continuous run of storefronts and homes above commercial premises. Compare the particular frontage rather than treat all Marina addresses as the same setting.
chestnut-street.characterHeading: A more continuous neighborhood storefront setting
character: Planning described a relatively continuous two-to-four-story commercial streetscape, generous storefront windows and housing above shops. Its 2013 comparison with Union Street documents two separate neighborhood-commercial environments, rather than interchangeable Marina labels.
chestnut-street.fit: Recurring neighborhood services and walk-in retail can test visibility along a more continuous storefront run. Food or fitness concepts should assess residential adjacency and the size of the actual premises.
chestnut-street.check: Count passersby at proposed operating hours, including weekdays and weekends. Observe legal loading and customer pickup at the exact frontage. Confirm use classification, ventilation, accessibility and any outdoor or evening-use approvals.
chestnut-street.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: Union Street offers a different commercial setting from nearby Chestnut: a more varied mix of building forms, specialty retail, services and restaurants. The shape of the individual premises can matter as much as the address.
union-street-cow-hollow.characterHeading: Different building forms, different premises choices
character: Planning’s 2013 corridor comparison describes Union as less uniform in built form than Chestnut, with retail, neighborhood services and restaurants drawing both local and visiting customers. This supports a distinct destination-and-neighborhood identity without proving current sales or footfall.
union-street-cow-hollow.fit: Specialty retail, wellness or appointment-based services should test destination access and repeat visits. Nonuniform building layouts make stairs, split levels and usable selling area relevant.
union-street-cow-hollow.check: Visit each block at appointment times and evening closing. Measure step-free entry, customer circulation and back-of-house capacity. Check pickup/loading rules and acoustic separation from housing.
union-street-cow-hollow.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: The Marina combines a residential neighborhood, Lombard-facing commercial activity and distinct shopping streets. A quieter side-street office and a visible corridor location call for different checks.
marina-district.characterHeading: Exposition history and a residential neighborhood
character: Planning’s centennial brochure documents the Marina’s relationship to the 1915 exposition and the subsequent residential land pattern. That neighborhood history is useful context, but it does not make waterfront recreation, Lombard traffic and Chestnut shopping equivalent business locations.
marina-district.fit: Small professional and customer-service offices can compare quieter side streets with Lombard visibility. Separate employee commutes from customer trips and event-related visits.
marina-district.check: Identify whether the candidate fronts Lombard, a residential street or a named retail corridor. Check noise, address visibility, step-free access and evening security arrangements. Validate seismic and building-condition records for the particular structure.
marina-district.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: A Mission District corridor where shops, services, food and housing share the street. Customer activity, bicycle access, deliveries and the exact frontage all matter to a prospective tenant.
valencia-street.characterHeading: A mixed-use corridor with changing curb arrangements
character: The Mission Area Plan places Valencia within a mixed-use pattern of shops, services, housing, small offices and production uses. SFMTA’s bikeway project describes the move toward side-running lanes and explicitly identifies parking/loading and parklet tradeoffs.
valencia-street.fit: Food, specialty and experiential concepts should assess day-to-evening activity at the specific block. A bicycle-accessible frontage still needs a workable supplier-delivery and customer-pickup plan.
valencia-street.check: Inspect current curb markings, parklets, delivery paths and bike-lane crossings. Confirm legal exhaust, refuse storage and late-hours conditions for a food or evening use. Test noise transmission to housing and compare weekday versus weekend visits.
valencia-street.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: Fillmore is not one interchangeable commercial strip. Start with the relevant segment and block, then compare the storefront, surrounding uses and the way customers arrive.
fillmore-street.characterHeading: Choose the segment before choosing the storefront
character: A 2022 Planning application at 2109 Fillmore documents a small retail unit within the Upper Fillmore neighborhood-commercial district. It is concrete evidence of fine-grained commercial premises and review of chain-store use, rather than evidence that a whole neighborhood has one tenant profile.
fillmore-street.fit: Boutiques, customer services and dining should compare the exact block’s shopping context and return-customer access. Small visible storefronts may trade selling-area efficiency for street presence.
fillmore-street.check: Confirm whether the address belongs to Upper Fillmore or another Fillmore segment. Check current formula-retail and proposed-use treatment for the actual operator. Test delivery windows, signage, accessibility and usable frontage.
fillmore-street.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: A neighborhood commercial corridor worth comparing for specialty shops, design-related businesses and planned customer visits. Separate an office, a showroom and customer-facing retail before looking at premises.
sacramento-street.characterHeading: Specialty commerce and the distinction between office and retail
character: A 2019 Planning case at 3419 Sacramento documents a design office with accessory retail in a mixed commercial/residential building. The 2021 Button Down report documents its move to the corridor in 1990. Together these support a history of specialty commerce, without certifying current tenants or permissions.
sacramento-street.fit: Design professionals and specialty sellers should distinguish customer-facing retail from office or showroom operations. Planned visits may matter more than assuming a large volume of incidental walk-ins.
sacramento-street.check: Obtain current confirmation of the precise proposed use, including accessory retail and floor level. Test appointment arrival, samples storage and delivery access. Confirm that the business model works without relying on an unmeasured footfall claim.
sacramento-street.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: A neighborhood commercial setting with a significant LGBTQ history and a prominent transit street. Community connections, customer arrival and the practicalities of operating on Market deserve equal attention.
upper-market-castro.characterHeading: Community history and a complex arrival pattern
character: The adopted Twin Peaks Tavern landmark report places the Castro within the development of visible LGBTQ community life. SFMTA documents Upper Market’s complex intersections and a safety project from Octavia to Castro, substantially completed in 2023. Community identity and street geometry both matter to location decisions.
upper-market-castro.fit: Neighborhood services, food and destination businesses should understand the community they serve and their operating hours. Market visibility does not establish an easy loading route or convenient crossing to a particular shop.
upper-market-castro.check: Walk the station-to-door route and inspect crossings and step-free access. Test delivery circulation and legal turns instead of assuming a direct vehicle approach. Check permitted entertainment/hours and residential sound separation.
upper-market-castro.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: A broad residential district with several distinct commercial clusters, including Geary, Clement and Balboa. Choose the corridor and cross-streets first; the Richmond label alone is too broad for a premises search.
richmond.characterHeading: Several commercial streets within a broad neighborhood
character: Planning’s Richmond Strategy describes early land-intensive uses followed by residential growth after the 1906 earthquake. It identifies commercial clusters on Geary, Clement and Balboa. Planning’s Chinese American history work also traces mid-century community development into the Richmond and Sunset.
richmond.fit: Neighborhood services, food and professional practices should select an actual commercial cluster before comparing spaces. A boulevard frontage and a smaller shopping street can imply different pedestrian arrival and visibility conditions.
richmond.check: Compare Inner/Outer location, exact cross-street and the real customer travel route. Observe crossing comfort, transit stops and loading for the candidate block. Check current occupancy costs and the customer area your business actually serves.
richmond.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: A residential district where commercial activity follows particular neighborhood and transit streets. A shop close to a rail stop offers a different arrival pattern from premises elsewhere in the district.
character: Planning’s adopted builder history links much of Sunset residential growth to streetcar tunnels and interwar homebuilding. SFMTA documents the L Taraval’s 1919 origins and completed 2021/2024 corridor upgrades. These histories explain a neighborhood commercial setting organized around specific transport streets.
sunset.fit: Local services and food concepts should define a repeat-customer catchment around the actual corridor. Rail access is relevant at a particular stop and walking route, not equally across the whole Sunset.
sunset.check: Walk from the nearest actual stop and compare travel times at staff shift hours. Inspect boarding islands, crossings and the legal supplier delivery location. Test block-level customer activity and weather exposure at planned opening hours.
sunset.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: A neighborhood where Third Street commerce and a significant African American cultural history sit alongside industrial and residential areas. A storefront search and an operational-industrial search should start with different requirements.
bayview.characterHeading: Third Street commerce and industrial neighbors
character: The City describes Third Street as a longstanding business district with significant African American civic and cultural history. The Area Plan separates neighborhood commerce from industrial functions and seeks to reduce conflicts between housing, trucks and industrial activity.
bayview.fit: Third Street customer-facing businesses should evaluate community-serving demand and access at the specific block. Neighborhood cultural identity is meaningful context, not a proxy for spending power or a guarantee of sales.
bayview.check: Distinguish Third Street storefronts from industrial parcels and residential side streets. Test station-to-door travel, daytime/evening activity and supplier approach. Verify the precise permitted use, building condition and nearby uses.
bayview.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: An operational business setting where production, distribution and repair requirements need to lead the search. District character is useful context; the building, vehicle access and permitted process determine whether a site is worth pursuing.
bayview-industrial.characterHeading: Industrial history, with parcel-specific operating requirements
character: The Bayview Area Plan recognizes the district’s industrial history and seeks to sustain industrial employment while reducing land-use conflicts. Its industrial, truck-route and environmental policies make operational compatibility central to a site decision. Historical plan maps and proposals need current parcel verification.
bayview-industrial.fit: Production, distribution, repair and food operations should lead with building systems and vehicle requirements. A district-level industrial identity does not establish that a particular site permits the process or has adequate power, loading or yard space.
bayview-industrial.check: Document truck dimensions, turning path, dock/grade access and legal delivery hours. Verify power, ventilation, fire protection, wastewater and any food/process permits. Review environmental history, flood/shoreline exposure and residential adjacency for the parcel.
bayview-industrial.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.

introduction: A waterfront area with maritime, rail and industrial roots, alongside changing mixed-use edges. Distinguish a working production site from an office-led conversion or a future development proposal.
central-waterfront.characterHeading: Working industry and changing mixed-use edges
character: The 2008 Area Plan recounts maritime, railroad and industrial development and distinguishes core industrial protection from mixed-use areas. Its policy framework accommodates selected office/R&D uses outside the core while resisting displacement of production, distribution and repair.
central-waterfront.fit: Fabrication and office-production hybrids should distinguish genuine operating floors from office-led adaptive reuse. Northern mixed-use amenities and redevelopment examples should not be generalized to operational blocks farther south.
central-waterfront.check: Confirm parcel zoning and whether the proposed office component is accessory or independently allowed. Verify floor loading, freight access, power, ventilation and truck circulation. Check contamination history and conflicts with nearby residential or visitor uses.
central-waterfront.geography: Compare the actual street and address. This guide and its map show approximate commercial context; they do not establish legal boundaries, permitted uses or available space.
